works.title: Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture Vol. 2: Patterns for Concurrent and Networked Objects
works.note: The route's naming catalog: defines Active Object, ACT, Half-Sync/Half-Async, Leader/Followers, Proactor, Reactor, TSS; its Reactor/Proactor chapters teach the event-demultiplexing loop at catalog grade.

works.title: Protothreads: Simplifying Event-Driven Programming of Memory-Constrained Embedded Systems
works.note: Naming paper and complete treatment of the protothread mechanism (stackless threads over local continuations in C).

works.title: Modern Embedded Systems Programming video course + QP framework docs
works.note: The course's later segments teach the Active Object model (event queue + private state + run-to-completion) as the central embedded concurrency discipline, with QP as the running realization.

works.title: Practical UML Statecharts in C/C++: Event-Driven Programming for Embedded Systems, 2nd ed.
works.note: Part II is a book-length treatment of the active-object (QP) framework for embedded C/C++ — the deepest embedded-side teaching of the element.

works.title: Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems
works.note: Names and specifies the Multi-State Task pattern within its time-triggered scheduler pattern language.

works.title: The Definitive Guide to ARM Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M4 Processors, 3rd ed.
works.note: NVIC chapters define nested interrupt handling (preemption priorities, tail-chaining, late-arrival) at register-level catalog grade.

works.title: What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory
works.note: Names false sharing and teaches the cache-line-padding/alignment countermeasure with measurements — the naming source for the element.

works.title: Java Concurrency in Practice
works.authors: Goetz, Peierls, Bloch, Bowbeer, Holmes, Lea
works.note: Canonical teaching text for task-execution mechanisms: the Executor framework (ch.6), applying thread pools (ch.8), and Future-based result handling; names Executor and Thread Pool for the catalog. Verified via InformIT publisher page.

works.title: Concurrent Programming in Java: Design Principles and Patterns, 2nd ed.
works.note: The pre-java.util.concurrent pattern catalog: worker threads (4.1.4), futures (4.3.3), fork/join parallel decomposition (4.4.1) — the design-pattern-level treatment behind JCiP's APIs. Verified via Lea's own supplement page (gee.cs.oswego.edu/dl/cpj).

works.title: Patterns for Parallel Programming
works.note: The parallel pattern language that names five route elements outright — SPMD, Loop Parallelism, Fork/Join, Master/Worker, Pipeline (ch.5 Supporting Structures; TOC confirmed on InformIT publisher page).

works.title: Structured Parallel Programming: Patterns for Efficient Computation
works.note: Modern deterministic-pattern treatment: map (loop parallelism), collectives/reduction (ch.5), stencil (ch.7), pipeline (ch.9) — the best current teaching of the data-parallel kernel shapes. Verified via Elsevier shop page with TOC.

works.title: Notes on structured concurrency, or: Go statement considered harmful
works.note: The essay that named and argued structured concurrency (nurseries); the acknowledged source behind Trio, Kotlin coroutine scopes, and JEP 453 (the latter kept as aka support only). Loaded live: title/author/date 2018-04-25 confirmed.

works.title: A Universal Modular ACTOR Formalism for Artificial Intelligence
works.note: Origin of the actor model, folded into active-object as aka support (actors = active entities with mailboxes). Title confirmed live in the official IJCAI 1973 proceedings listing.

works.title: Debugging Optimized Code with Dynamic Deoptimization
works.note: The paper that introduced dynamic deoptimization (in the Self VM) — the naming source and still the definitive mechanism description. Verified live via the official Self project bibliography (bibliography.selflanguage.org) incl. full citation.

works.title: HotSpot Glossary of Terms
works.note: Authoritative living definition of deoptimization in the production VM that mainstreamed it (uncommon traps, nmethod invalidation); definition quoted live this session.

works.title: Threaded Code
works.unresolved: doi/pages — ACM DL Cloudflare-blocked this session; citation cross-checked only via Ertl's academic threaded-code bibliography (bell73, CACM, received June)
works.note: The CACM note that named threaded code; canon for interpreter dispatch technique naming.

works.title: Threaded Code (what is threaded code, direct/indirect threading, dispatch techniques)
works.note: The standing modern treatment of threaded-code dispatch (direct/indirect/token threading, computed goto) by the field's principal researcher; loaded live.

works.title: Design of a Separable Transition-Diagram Compiler
works.note: The paper that coined 'coroutine'. Verified live on the author's own site: melconway.com/Home/Inventor.html cites 'Comm. ACM 6 (July 1963), 396' and hosts the scanned PDF.

works.title: Revisiting Coroutines
works.note: The modern canonical survey/formalization of coroutines (full asymmetric coroutines, expressiveness vs one-shot continuations) — the best current treatment pairing Conway's 1963 naming. Citation incl. DOI confirmed live on Ierusalimschy's publications page.

works.title: Crafting Interpreters
works.note: Part III builds a complete bytecode virtual machine (clox) — the catalog-grade teaching text that names the element; official site loaded live (ISBN confirmed).

works.title: Game Programming Patterns
works.note: Names and teaches Game Loop (Sequencing Patterns) and Bytecode (Behavioral Patterns) as design patterns; site + full contents page loaded live confirming both chapters and ISBN.

works.title: Game Engine Architecture, 4th ed. (two-volume set)
works.note: The engine text whose concurrency chapters define the fiber-based job system (element named from the 3rd ed's job-system chapter; current edition verified live on gameenginebook.com incl. hardware-parallelism/concurrency coverage) and the frame/game loop.

works.title: Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions
works.note: Names Competing Consumers (multiple consumers on one point-to-point channel for concurrent message processing); pattern page on the official EIP site loaded live with ISBN.

works.title: Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture, Volume 1: A System of Patterns
works.note: Names the Master-Slave design pattern (divide work among identical slaves, master combines results); Wiley product page loaded live confirming authors, ISBN, August 1996.

works.title: The F# Asynchronous Programming Model
works.note: The paper behind async/await: F# async workflows, the direct ancestor of C# await and the JS/Python/Rust async models; Springer chapter page loaded live confirming title and DOI.

works.title: Promises: Linguistic Support for Efficient Asynchronous Procedure Calls in Distributed Systems
works.unresolved: doi/pages — ACM DL Cloudflare-blocked and PMG CSAIL unreachable this session; identifier not confirmed against a primary page
works.note: Canonical naming paper for promises/futures as first-class results of asynchronous calls; kept despite failed live check because it is the element's naming canon.

works.title: Trampolined Style
works.note: Names trampolined style: a single scheduler loop stepping suspended computations — the canon for the trampoline element. Full citation + abstract confirmed live on Mitchell Wand's own bibliography page (ccs.neu.edu).

works.title: Patterns in Java, Volume 1: A Catalog of Reusable Design Patterns Illustrated with UML
works.unresolved: isbn — Wiley product page is client-rendered and exposed no bibliographic payload this session; 1st-ed ISBN not confirmed on a primary page
works.note: The pattern catalog that names Two-Phase Termination among its concurrency patterns; only catalog-grade source naming the element.

works.title: Is Parallel Programming Hard, And, If So, What Can You Do About It?
works.note: The kernel-school concurrency book: parallel fastpath designs (McKenney's own PLoPD2 lineage), per-thread/per-CPU data ownership, and cache-line/false-sharing effects — modern treatment for three route elements. Official kernel.org page loaded live.

works.title: The Node.js Event Loop (Event Loop, Timers, and process.nextTick)
works.note: Catalog-grade official teaching of the event-loop mechanism (phases: timers, poll, check, close; microtask queue) — upgrades the element from its bare-Wikipedia naming. Loaded live.

works.title: JEP 444: Virtual Threads
works.note: Authoritative modern treatment of user-mode (green) threads: explicitly contrasts historical M:1 green threads, 1:1 platform threads, and M:N virtual threads — upgrades the element from its bare-Wikipedia naming. Loaded live (title + green-threads discussion confirmed).

works.title: Restartable sequences
works.note: The naming article for restartable sequences (per-CPU critical sections with kernel-assisted restart, later the rseq(2) syscall); title/author/date 2015-07-07 confirmed live.

works.title: Cancellation in Managed Threads
works.note: The authoritative treatment of the cancellation-token mechanism: CancellationTokenSource/CancellationToken, cooperative polling/callback/wait-handle listening, linked tokens. Loaded live in full.

notes: All 37 r4 elements covered by >=1 catalog-grade work; no gaps. Membership seeds: posa2, protothreads, samekcourse confirmed; freertosbook REJECTED for this route (its task/queue/ISR material maps to other routes' elements; it defines no r4 element at catalog grade); pont, yiu, dreppermem, samekbook added as further memberships from the route file's own named_in fields. Both Wikipedia-only-named elements upgraded to authoritative treatments (event-loop -> Node.js official docs; green-threads -> JEP 444). Old naming sources paired with modern treatments per mission rule (Conway 1963 + Revisiting Coroutines 2009; Hoelzle 1992 + HotSpot Glossary; Bell 1973 + Ertl's living threaded-code page; McKenney PLoPD2 fastpath subsumed by perfbook, same author). JEP 453/Kotlin left as aka support per seed guidance; Agha 1986 dropped in favor of Hewitt 1973 (MIT Press and DSpace both bot-blocked; IJCAI-73 official proceedings verified). 3 of 26 new works unverified: bellthreaded (ACM DL Cloudflare-blocked; cross-checked via Ertl bibliography), liskovpromises (ACM DL blocked, PMG CSAIL unreachable), grandjava (Wiley page client-rendered, no bibliographic payload) — each kept because it is the element's naming canon, with the soft field named. Gregory GEA cited at the live-verified 4th ed (2026, gameenginebook.com); the job-system naming stems from the 3rd ed's chapter, noted in the entry.
